11. (Currently Amended) A method comprising:administering a concentration of magnetic nanoparticles and a concentration of bindable agents to a test sample, wherein the test sample comprises a biofluid to be tested for a disease component and each of the bindable agents are configured to attach to a plurality of the magnetic nanoparticles and the disease component;
transmitting a light beam through the test sample to a light detector;establishing a magnetic field gradient through the test sample; andSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1370.187
determining whether a disease component exists in the test sample when a change in intensity of the transmitted light beam under the magnetic field gradient exhibits a variable intensity change pattern during a time period[[l wherein the determining comprises matching the change in intensity to a predetermined pattern.
12. (Canceled)
13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim [[12]] wherein the predetermined pattern is established based on the disease.SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.140.20
14. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the bindable agents are configured to attach to the disease component in the test sample to tag the disease component in the sample with the magnetic nanoparticles.
15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14, wherein a radius of the disease component is much greater than a radius of one of the magnetic nanoparticles attached to the bindable agentt and wherein a drift speed of the disease component bound to the bindable agent attached to at least one of the magnetic nanoparticles in a presence of the magnetic field gradient is much greater than a drift speed of the one of the magnetic nanoparticles attached to the bindable agent in the presence of the magnetic field gradient.SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.100.05
16. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the disease component is a bacteria, a virus, a fungus, or a cancer cell.
17. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the bindable agent is an antibody specific for the disease component, a ligand specific for the disease component, or an aptimer specific to the disease component.
18. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 11, further comprising diagnosing a disease or condition in a patient based on the disease component existing in the test sample.
19. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 18, wherein the diagnosing further comprises performing a differential analysis on the test sample when the disease component exists in the test sample to diagnose the disease or condition.
20. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the magnetic field is established between two magnets so that the resultant magnetic field lines are perpendicular to the light beam.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the variable intensity change pattern is based on a drift speed of the disease component tagged by the large number plurality of magnetic nanoparticles being at least an order of magnitude greater than a drift speed of unbound magnetic nanoparticles.
